messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: ADIC: auto diff for c sources?
parts:
Hi!

I just found ADIC: http://www.mcs.anl.gov/research/projects/adic/

It is a pity that the license is not usable for Stan (maybe someone else has a look). But apart from that, the ADIC systems sounds amazing - you give it a piece of C source code and it generates you a c source code which gives you the partial derivatives. Having this, in particular, for the ODE integrator would be stunning.

Maybe there are similar systems out there already which have a better license?

Cheers,
Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ADIC: auto diff for c sources?
parts:
We've thought about code generation off and on. It's what
Theano (Python) does.

The problem is conditionals and branching. If we could get
rid of all of those, code generation is a no-brainer. But if
we'd done that, we woudn't have many of our matrix algorithms
and would've taken a lot longer to get ODEs out, etc.

We may still think about more in the future if we could
limit Stan's language's expressiveness.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ADIC: auto diff for c sources?
parts:
clad is just forward mode, which isn't so useful. Stan's C++
templates do efficient forward mode, so you don't need to code
generate (or maybe I should say is that the template system gives
you all you need to code generate).

We need reverse mode for efficient gradients O(1) relative to
function evaluation rather than O(N) in forward mode.

- Bob

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ADIC: auto diff for c sources?
parts:
Hi!

I am assuming here that doing code-generation will speed up the gradients considerably since the compiler can then take this code and make it optimized. Under this assumption: Is it thinkable to restrict the ODE system function in what is allowed and what not and do code generation for that? I mean, most ODE system functions are algebraically really simple and doing AD (which is great for its generality) is overkill.

I think even a much restricted set of operations which are allowed in a ODE system function would cover many cases. But of course, doing this "just" for ODEs... not sure.

Sebastian

PS: That this is a nobrainer to you... amazing. This looks like it would kill me.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ADIC: auto diff for c sources?
parts:
I meant that it'd be a no-brainer that we should do it that way,
not that it'd be easy to do! Basically, compile everything up
front that can be compiled. Code generation would follow the
way that autodiff works now. But we have lots of functions, so
it'd be a huge pain to get it going.

I don't want to make a restricted subsystem of things just
for ODEs. We have toyed with restricting all of Stan so we
could do this everywhere.

- Bob
